title: Past, experience, plans
goal: Say what you did, what you've done before and what you plan to do, and give reasons and opinions.

notes.p: {{咗|zo2}} right after the verb means the action is done. To ask 'yet?', put {{未|mei6}} at the end: {{你食咗飯未呀？|nei5 sik6 zo2 faan6 mei6 aa3}} (a friendly greeting too). Say yes with the verb and {{咗|zo2}}: {{食咗喇|sik6 zo2 laa3}}. Say no with {{未呀|mei6 aa3}}, or put {{未|mei6}} before the verb and drop {{咗|zo2}}: {{我未食|ngo5 mei6 sik6}}.
ex: nei5 sik6 zo2 faan6 mei6 aa3

notes.p: {{過|gwo3}} after a verb means you have done it at some time: experience. Compare {{佢去咗香港|keoi5 heoi3 zo2 hoeng1 gong2}} 'she has gone to Hong Kong' (she's there now) with {{佢去過香港|keoi5 heoi3 gwo3 hoeng1 gong2}} 'she has been to Hong Kong before'. Not yet: {{我未去過|ngo5 mei6 heoi3 gwo3}}. Sound tip: {{咗|zo2}} rises, {{過|gwo3}} stays mid and level.
ex: nei5 heoi3 gwo3 hoeng1 gong2 mei6 aa3
Have you been to Hong Kong?
She has gone to Hong Kong (she's there now).

notes.p: {{會|wui5}} = will, for predictions. {{想|soeng2}} = want to. {{打算|daa2 syun3}} = plan to. All three go straight before the verb. Cantonese has no tense: time words like {{聽日|ting1 jat6}} tell you when.
ex: I want to go to Hong Kong.
ngo5 daa2 syun3 sing1 kei4 luk6 heoi3 haang4 gaai1
I'm planning to go shopping on Saturday.

notes.p: {{因為|jan1 wai6}} = because and {{所以|so2 ji5}} = so; use one or both, the reason comes first. {{如果|jyu4 gwo2}} = if; in the second half, {{就|zau6}} 'then' goes right before the verb. {{不如…啦|bat1 jyu4 … laa1}} = 'how about…', a friendly suggestion.
ex: 因為落緊雨，所以我哋搭的士
jan1 wai6 lok6 gan2 jyu5, so2 ji5 ngo5 dei6 daap3 dik1 si2
Because it's raining, we're taking a taxi.
如果落雨，我哋就搭的士
jyu4 gwo2 lok6 jyu5, ngo5 dei6 zau6 daap3 dik1 si2
If it rains, we'll take a taxi.
bat1 jyu4 ngo5 dei6 heoi3 sik6 faan6 laa1

notes.p: {{覺得|gok3 dak1}} = think or feel (an opinion). {{得|dak1}} after a verb is followed by how well it's done: {{講得好好|gong2 dak1 hou2 hou2}}. {{同|tung4}} = with; it goes before the verb, not at the end: {{我同朋友去咗飲茶|ngo5 tung4 pang4 jau5 heoi3 zo2 jam2 caa4}}.
ex: ngo5 gok3 dak1 hou2 hou2 sik6
nei5 gwong2 dung1 waa2 gong2 dak1 hou2 hou2
ngo5 tung4 pang4 jau5 heoi3 zo2 jam2 caa4
I went for dim sum with friends.

vocab.note: 咗 (zo2) after a verb = the action is done.

t: nei5 sik6 zo2 faan6 mei6 aa3
vocab.note: A friendly greeting, like "how's it going?". 未 (mei6) at the end = "yet?"
過 (gwo3) after a verb = "have ever done".

ngo5 gwong2 dung1 waa2 gong2 dak1 m4 hai6 gei2 hou2
m4 hou2 ji3 si1, ngo5 ci4 zo2 siu2 siu2
ngo5 dei6 gei2 dim2 gin3 aa3
ngo5 aan3 di1 daa2 bei2 nei5
nei5 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 bong1 ngo5 aa3
ngo5 gok3 dak1 hou2 hou2 sik6
vocab.note: 覺得 (gok3 dak1) = to think / feel (an opinion).

vocab.en: What did you do this weekend?

t: ngo5 tung4 pang4 jau5 heoi3 zo2 jam2 caa4
vocab.en: I went for dim sum with friends

t: ni1 go3 hai6 bin1 go3 ge3

vocab.note: {{未|mei6}} before the verb = not yet. No {{咗|zo2}} here.
Goes before the verb: {{我打算去|ngo5 daa2 syun3 heoi3}}.
Not the same as {{你點呀？|nei5 dim2 aa3}} 'how are you?'.
Before the verb: {{同朋友去|tung4 pang4 jau5 heoi3}}.
Goes right before the verb in the second half: {{我哋就去|ngo5 dei6 zau6 heoi3}}.

items.why: {{咗|zo2}} marks a finished action; {{喇|laa3}} adds 'already'.
{{未|mei6}} at the end asks 'yet?': {{食咗飯未呀？|sik6 zo2 faan6 mei6 aa3}}.
{{過|gwo3}} after a verb = have done it before. {{去緊|heoi3 gan2}} would be 'on the way'.

items.en: I haven't been to Hong Kong yet.
items.why: {{未|mei6}} before the verb = not yet: {{未去過|mei6 heoi3 gwo3}}. {{唔|m4}} can't be used with {{過|gwo3}}.
{{會|wui5}} = will, a prediction. {{想|soeng2}} is 'want to', {{識|sik1}} is 'know how to'.

q: ngo5 hou2 gui6, ___ soeng2 faan1 uk1 kei2
items.en: I'm tired, so I want to go home.
items.why: {{所以|so2 ji5}} = so. With {{因為|jan1 wai6}} it would say you're tired because you want to go home.

q: ___你得閒，我哋就一齊去睇戲啦
___ nei5 dak1 haan4, ngo5 dei6 zau6 jat1 cai4 heoi3 tai2 hei3 laa1
items.en: If you're free, let's go see a movie together.
items.why: {{如果|jyu4 gwo2}} = if, and {{就|zau6}} in the second half means 'then'.

q: ___ ngo5 dei6 heoi3 sik6 faan6 laa1
items.why: {{不如…啦|bat1 jyu4 … laa1}} = how about…

q: nei5 gwong2 dung1 waa2 gong2 ___ hou2 hou2
items.why: Verb + {{得|dak1}} + how well: {{講得好好|gong2 dak1 hou2 hou2}}, 'speak really well'.

q: ngo5 ___ pang4 jau5 heoi3 zo2 jam2 caa4
items.en: I went for dim sum with friends.
items.why: {{同|tung4}} = with, and it comes before the verb.
{{覺得|gok3 dak1}} = think, feel (an opinion).

q: nei5 zau1 mut6 zou6 ___ di1 me1 aa3
items.en: What did you do on the weekend?
items.why: {{做咗|zou6 zo2}} = did. Asking what happened takes {{咗|zo2}}.

q: m4 hou2 ji3 si1, ngo5 ci4 ___ siu2 siu2
items.why: English says 'I'm late', but Cantonese says 'I have become late': {{遲咗|ci4 zo2}}.
{{到|dou3}} (mid level) = arrive. {{度|dou6}}, {{都|dou1}} and {{島|dou2}} differ only in tone.
{{晏啲|aan3 di1}} = a bit later. {{平啲|peng4 di1}} is cheaper, {{近啲|kan5 di1}} closer.

q: ngo5 baa4 baa1 heoi3 ___ hoeng1 gong2
items.en: My dad has gone to Hong Kong (he's there now).
items.why: {{去咗|heoi3 zo2}} = has gone and is there now. {{去過|heoi3 gwo3}} = has been there at some time before.

items.q: Auntie asks {{你食咗飯未呀？|nei5 sik6 zo2 faan6 mei6 aa3}} You haven't eaten yet. You say:
items.why: A {{未|mei6}} question is answered 'not yet' with {{未呀|mei6 aa3}}. {{食咗喇|sik6 zo2 laa3}} would mean you have eaten; {{唔食|m4 sik6}} means you don't (want to) eat.

items.q: You arrive ten minutes late to meet Wing. You say:
opts: m4 hou2 ji3 si1, ngo5 ci4 zo2 siu2 siu2
m4 goi1, ngo5 ci4 zo2 siu2 siu2
m4 hou2 ji3 si1, ngo5 ci4 gan2 siu2 siu2
do1 ze6, ngo5 ci4 zo2 siu2 siu2
items.why: Apologise with {{唔好意思|m4 hou2 ji3 si1}}; being late takes {{咗|zo2}}.

items.q: Mr Chan says {{你廣東話講得好好！|nei5 gwong2 dung1 waa2 gong2 dak1 hou2 hou2}} You thank him and modestly say you don't speak it very well:
opts: do1 ze6! ngo5 gong2 dak1 m4 hai6 gei2 hou2
m4 goi1! ngo5 gong2 dak1 m4 hai6 gei2 hou2
do1 ze6! ngo5 gong2 gan2 m4 hai6 gei2 hou2
m4 hou2 ji3 si1! ngo5 gong2 dak1 hou2 hou2
items.why: A compliment gets {{多謝|do1 ze6}}, not {{唔該|m4 goi1}}. How well you speak needs {{講得|gong2 dak1}}.

items.q: You want to suggest to your friends that you all go for dim sum. You say:
opts: bat1 jyu4 ngo5 dei6 heoi3 jam2 caa4 laa1
bat1 jyu4 ngo5 dei6 heoi3 zo2 jam2 caa4 laa1
jyu4 gwo2 ngo5 dei6 heoi3 jam2 caa4 laa1
ngo5 dei6 heoi3 gwo3 jam2 caa4 laa1
items.why: {{不如…啦|bat1 jyu4 … laa1}} makes a suggestion. A suggestion is about the future, so no {{咗|zo2}} or {{過|gwo3}}.

items.q: You visited Hong Kong once, years ago. A friend asks {{你去過香港未呀？|nei5 heoi3 gwo3 hoeng1 gong2 mei6 aa3}} You answer:
items.why: Answer by repeating the verb with {{過|gwo3}}: {{去過|heoi3 gwo3}}, 'I have been'.

items.q: The forecast says rain tomorrow. You tell your wife:
items.why: {{聽日|ting1 jat6}} tomorrow + {{會|wui5}} will. {{尋日|cam4 jat6}} is yesterday.

items.q: A friend asks why you're taking a taxi. It's raining. You explain:
opts: 因為落緊雨，所以我搭的士
jan1 wai6 lok6 gan2 jyu5, so2 ji5 ngo5 daap3 dik1 si2
所以落緊雨，因為我搭的士
so2 ji5 lok6 gan2 jyu5, jan1 wai6 ngo5 daap3 dik1 si2
如果落緊雨，所以我搭的士
jyu4 gwo2 lok6 gan2 jyu5, so2 ji5 ngo5 daap3 dik1 si2
點解落緊雨，所以我搭的士
dim2 gaai2 lok6 gan2 jyu5, so2 ji5 ngo5 daap3 dik1 si2
items.why: {{因為|jan1 wai6}} goes with the reason, {{所以|so2 ji5}} with the result.

items.q: You tell a friend that you're planning to go to Hong Kong with your wife. You say:
opts: ngo5 daa2 syun3 tung4 lou5 po4 heoi3 hoeng1 gong2
我打算同老婆去咗香港
ngo5 daa2 syun3 tung4 lou5 po4 heoi3 zo2 hoeng1 gong2
ngo5 daa2 syun3 lou5 po4 tung4 heoi3 hoeng1 gong2
我打算同老婆去過香港
ngo5 daa2 syun3 tung4 lou5 po4 heoi3 gwo3 hoeng1 gong2
items.why: {{同|tung4}} comes before the person. A plan hasn't happened yet, so no {{咗|zo2}} or {{過|gwo3}}.

ngo5 hok6 gan2 gwong2 dung1 waa2

opts: I want to go to Hong Kong.
I'm on my way to Hong Kong.
I haven't been to Hong Kong.
Have you been to Hong Kong?
items.why: {{去過|heoi3 gwo3}} = have been. Want to go would be {{想去|soeng2 heoi3}}.
{{聽日|ting1 jat6}} tomorrow, {{會|wui5}} will, {{落雨|lok6 jyu5}} rain.
{{未|mei6}} = not yet. 'I don't eat that' would use {{唔|m4}}.

opts: I went for dim sum with friends.

items.why: {{同朋友|tung4 pang4 jau5}} with friends; {{去咗|heoi3 zo2}} went.
{{啱啱|ngaam1 ngaam1}} = just now; {{到|dou3}} = arrive. On its own, {{啱|ngaam1}} means 'that's right'.

say: ngo5 aan3 di1 daa2 bei2 nei5
opts: I'll give it to you later.
items.why: {{打俾你|daa2 bei2 nei5}} = call you. Without {{打|daa2}}, {{俾你|bei2 nei5}} would be 'give you'.
{{覺得|gok3 dak1}} = think. Without it, {{你點呀？|nei5 dim2 aa3}} is 'how are you?'.

s: 你食咗飯未呀？
nei5 sik6 zo2 faan6 mei6 aa3

turns.why: Yes = {{食咗喇|sik6 zo2 laa3}}. {{未|mei6}} never goes together with {{咗|zo2}} in an answer.

s: 我都食咗喇。你今日做咗啲咩呀？
ngo5 dou1 sik6 zo2 laa3. nei5 gam1 jat6 zou6 zo2 di1 me1 aa3

ngo5 lou5 po4 tung4 heoi3 zo2 haang4 gaai1
ngo5 tung4 lou5 po4 heoi3 gwo3 zo2 haang4 gaai1
turns.why: {{同|tung4}} goes before the person: {{同老婆|tung4 lou5 po4}}. Use one aspect marker, not two.

s: 你覺得香港點呀？
nei5 gok3 dak1 hoeng1 gong2 dim2 aa3

ngo5 gok3 dak1 hou2 zeng3 zo2

m4 hou2 ji3 si1, ngo5 ci4 gan2 siu2 siu2
m4 hou2 ji3 si1, ngo5 ci4 gwo3 siu2 siu2
turns.why: Being late is said with {{咗|zo2}}: {{遲咗|ci4 zo2}}.

s: 唔緊要。你食咗飯未呀？
m4 gan2 jiu3. nei5 sik6 zo2 faan6 mei6 aa3

opts: 未呀，不如我哋去食飯啦

未呀，如果我哋去食飯啦

s: 好呀！你想食咩呀？
hou2 aa3! nei5 soeng2 sik6 me1 aa3
turns.en: Sure! What do you want to eat?

opts: ngo5 soeng2 sik6 caa1 siu1 baau1
ngo5 soeng2 sik6 zo2 caa1 siu1 baau1
ngo5 sik6 gwo3 caa1 siu1 baau1
turns.why: {{想|soeng2}} + verb for what you want to do. Wanting is about now, so no {{咗|zo2}}; {{食過|sik6 gwo3}} means you've had it before.

s: 你週末做咗啲咩呀？
nei5 zau1 mut6 zou6 zo2 di1 me1 aa3
turns.en: What did you do on the weekend?

opts: ngo5 tung4 pang4 jau5 heoi3 zo2 jam2 caa4
ngo5 tung4 pang4 jau5 heoi3 jam2 caa4 gan2
ngo5 tung4 pang4 jau5 heoi3 gwo3 zo2 jam2 caa4
turns.why: Something you did: {{去咗|heoi3 zo2}}. One marker only, right after the verb.

s: 好正！好唔好食呀？
hou2 zeng3! hou2 m4 hou2 sik6 aa3

opts: ngo5 gok3 dak1 hou2 hou2 sik6
ngo5 gok3 dak1 hou2 m4 hou2 sik6
ngo5 hou2 hou2 sik6 gok3 dak1
turns.why: {{覺得|gok3 dak1}} comes before the opinion. {{好唔好食|hou2 m4 hou2 sik6}} is the question, not the answer.

s: 下次我哋一齊去啦！
haa6 ci3 ngo5 dei6 jat1 cai4 heoi3 laa1

opts: 好呀！如果我得閒，我就去
hou2 aa3! jyu4 gwo2 ngo5 dak1 haan4, ngo5 zau6 heoi3

hou2 aa3! jyu4 gwo2 ngo5 dak1 haan4, so2 ji5 ngo5 heoi3

s: 你去過香港未呀？
nei5 heoi3 gwo3 hoeng1 gong2 mei6 aa3
turns.en: Have you been to Hong Kong?

mei6 aa3, ngo5 hou2 soeng2 heoi3 zo2
m4 aa3, ngo5 hou2 soeng2 heoi3
turns.why: 'Not yet' is {{未呀|mei6 aa3}}. Wanting to go is about the future, so no {{咗|zo2}}.

ngo5 daa2 syun3 lou5 po4 tung4 heoi3
ngo5 tung4 daa2 syun3 lou5 po4 heoi3
turns.why: Same order as his question: {{打算|daa2 syun3}} + {{同|tung4}} + person + verb.

nei5 gwong2 dung1 waa2 gong2 dak1 hou2 hou2

m4 goi1! ngo5 hok6 gan2 gwong2 dung1 waa2

roleplay.title: Monday morning catch-up
roleplay.setup: It's Monday morning and a Hong Kong friend asks about your weekend. Tell her what you did, give your opinion, and suggest a plan.
roleplay.persona: You are Ka-yan, a friendly Hong Kong woman in her late twenties who works in an office. Ask what the learner did at the weekend, who they went with, what they thought of it, and whether they've ever been to places or tried foods you mention (dim sum, milk tea, BBQ pork buns). Say what you did yourself (you went for dim sum with your mum and watched a movie). React to their suggestions. Speak simple colloquial Hong Kong Cantonese using mostly words from levels 1-6: 咗, 過, 未, 覺得, 同, 不如…啦, 因為/所以. Keep sentences short and repeat or slow down when asked.
opening: 早晨！你週末做咗啲咩呀？
zou2 san4! nei5 zau1 mut6 zou6 zo2 di1 me1 aa3
roleplay.opening_en: Morning! What did you do at the weekend?
goals: Say what you did and who with
Say whether you've ever done something she mentions

roleplay.title: Planning a Hong Kong trip
roleplay.setup: A Hong Kong-born friend of the family in Chicago asks about your plans to visit Hong Kong. Talk about whether you've been, who you'll go with and what you want to do.
roleplay.persona: You are Mr Chan, a warm Hong Kong man in his fifties who has lived in Chicago for twenty years. Ask whether the learner has been to Hong Kong, who they plan to go with, what they want to do and eat there. Mention that Hong Kong will be hot and it will often rain in summer, and suggest going for dim sum. Ask why they are learning Cantonese. Speak simple colloquial Hong Kong Cantonese using mostly words from levels 1-6: 過, 未, 會, 想, 打算, 因為…所以…, 如果…就…, 不如…啦. Short sentences.

roleplay.opening_en: Have you been to Hong Kong?
goals: Say who you plan to go with
Say what you want to do there
Give a reason with because or so
